Author:     Jakub Skokan <jakub.skokan@havefun.cz>
AuthorDate: Sat Oct 24 14:03:14 2026 +0200
Commit:     Jakub Skokan <jakub.skokan@havefun.cz>
CommitDate: Sat Oct 24 19:24:07 2026 +0200

    Guard automated input updates with cached Git ancestry
    
    Automated flake updates can replace manually pinned commits with revisions
    that do not contain them, including dependencies behind nested follows.
    
    Add an explicit forward-only transaction that prepares a separate Nix lock,
    checks the complete logical input graph and validates ancestry before
    installing or committing. Preserve the checkout on rejection or missing
    evidence, detect concurrent changes and keep existing manual update behavior.
    
    Use the existing full Git mirror cache for immutable GitHub commit proofs.
    Install cold mirrors atomically, fetch missing SHAs and serialize evidence
    and changelog reads with a shared URL lock. Reject insufficient or redirected
    history and keep ordinary Git transport configuration with safe errors.
    
    Expose the same policy for final committed-lock validation and full resolved
    JSON revisions for consumers. Document failure statuses, cache recovery and
    the limits of ancestry preservation.

    Keep packaged Ruby startup independent of caller preloads
    
    A development shell can set RUBYOPT to load its Bundler environment.
    Starting packaged confctl in that shell then activates the caller bundle
    with confctl's Ruby and gems, preventing even input listing.
    
    Disable RUBYOPT parsing only for the package interpreter. Keep RubyGems and
    the caller environment available to child commands so Git hooks can load
    their own bundle. Cover startup and a real Ruby pre-commit hook with a
    caller-bundle fixture, and document the startup boundary.

+## Guarded automated updates
+
+Use `--forward-only` in publishing workflows to retain manually pinned commits
+until the upstream branch contains them:
+
+```bash
+confctl inputs update --forward-only nixpkgs
+confctl inputs update --forward-only --all
+confctl inputs channel update --forward-only --commit --no-changelog \
+  '{production,staging}' nixpkgs
+confctl inputs machine update --forward-only --commit build.example.org nixpkgs
+```
+
+Options must come before positional arguments. The guard requires an existing
+version-7 `flake.lock` tracked in Git and a clean tracked checkout and index.
+Use a checkout with one writer. Cooperating guarded confctl updates use a
+process lock; other tools must not write to the checkout concurrently.
+
+Guarded updates require Nix 2.19 or newer, including
+`--reference-lock-file` and `--output-lock-file` support. The transaction and
+nested selection have been exercised with Nix 2.34.9. The packaged confctl uses
+its bundled Nix; installing another Nix in CI does not necessarily change that
+runtime. Unsupported flags or unmatched selectors fail without updating the
+real lock. There is no fallback to an update in place.
+
+The Nix package starts confctl with its packaged Ruby gems and ignores inherited
+`RUBYOPT` options for that Ruby process. It retains `RUBYOPT` and `BUNDLE_*`
+environment variables for child commands, including Git hooks. User scripts
+that explicitly load Bundler remain subject to their bundle configuration.
+
+confctl resolves requested `follows` aliases to their terminal input paths and
+deduplicates shared targets. For example, a root `nixpkgs` following
+`vpsadminos/nixpkgs`, where `vpsadminos` follows `vpsadmin/vpsadminos`, updates
+`vpsadmin/vpsadminos/nixpkgs`. It leaves both parent revisions unchanged.
+
+Nix writes a candidate lock beside the original flake, using a separate snapshot
+of the old lock as its reference. confctl validates the complete reachable
+graph before atomically installing the candidate. It compares logical dependency
+paths, including descendants and aliases, rather than generated node IDs. A
+forward root update that regresses a nested dependency is rejected as a whole.
+Local lock bytes, root `flake.nix`, Git HEAD, index entries and tracked checkout
+state are checked again before installation. No commit runs before acceptance.
+
+Each existing Git revision must equal or be an ancestor of its replacement in
+the same supported source. Currently the ancestry provider supports
+`github.com` sources with full immutable Git revisions, including
+`flake = false` sources. It checks commit ancestry with Git using the same full
+repository mirrors as changelogs. It does not use GitHub's compare API or read
+API tokens. Git's ordinary URL and authentication configuration remains in
+effect; inaccessible sources are evidence errors. Nix resolves the candidate
+separately and may still use GitHub APIs through its own fetcher.
+
+Mirrors are stored in `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/confctl/git-mirrors`.
+Each directory is named by the SHA256 digest of its exact source URL, preserving
+the existing cache layout and URL spelling. A cold comparison clones a full
+mirror; a warm comparison reuses both exact commit objects when present and
+fetches only missing full SHAs. A cold nixpkgs mirror can require substantial
+disk space and time. Persist this cache between CI runs; a cache miss never
+bypasses validation. `check-update` uses the same cache and may clone or fetch,
+while leaving both supplied lockfiles and the checkout untouched.
+
+A sibling lock file serializes initialization, fetching and reads for each URL,
+including changelog reads. New mirrors are installed atomically after successful
+cloning and validation. Existing shallow, partial, grafted, externally backed,
+wrong-origin or malformed mirrors fail with the cache key in the error. They
+are not automatically deleted, repaired or replaced; diagnose the reported
+entry and arrange recovery separately. Cached objects must be exact commits,
+not tags, trees or blobs. A negative ancestry result requires a successful walk
+of both tips' complete commit-parent history. Missing history and Git failures
+remain errors. Replacement objects and inherited repository redirection cannot
+alter the proof.
+
+The cache and ordinary Git configuration belong to the invoking user; this is
+not protection against a hostile writer with that user's access. Older confctl
+and manual Git writers do not honor the new lock. Reuse their full mirrors
+sequentially, without concurrent old/new writers. Mirror locks are released
+before commit hooks run. Changelog failures retain their existing soft error
+behavior; they cannot turn a failed ancestry check into an accepted update.
+
+Source, fetcher or extraction changes require manual review. A change to locked
+attributes at the same revision also rejects, including a changed `narHash`.
+Previously reachable paths cannot disappear. New paths must contain supported
+immutable Git sources. Unchanged unsupported sources may remain; changed path,
+tarball, indirect or other unsupported sources fail with an evidence error.
+The check does not prove that live path-source contents stayed unchanged.
+Changing the original branch/ref declaration alone is not a source-content
+change when the locked source is identical.
+
+A rejection or evidence error leaves the original lock, index and HEAD
+untouched by confctl. Nix failures, malformed candidates, cached GitHub metadata
+fallback warnings and unavailable ancestry evidence all stop the update.
+Concurrent checkout changes stop installation and are left for the writer to
+reconcile. A commit-hook failure after installation returns failure and leaves
+the validated candidate in place; hook side effects are not rolled back.
+Each invocation is a separate transaction: earlier local commits from a
+multi-command job are not undone when a later invocation fails.
+
+Exit status is `0` for an accepted update or no change, `3` for a known policy
+rejection, and `1` for missing or unsupported evidence and tool errors. Both
+nonzero statuses must stop publication. `--downgrade` only changes changelog
+direction and cannot bypass `--forward-only`. Unflagged manual updates and
+`inputs set` retain their existing behavior for deliberate revision changes.
+
+Ancestry preservation retains the pinned commit in history. It does not detect
+later reverts, prove patch equivalence after a cherry pick, or establish software
+compatibility. Keep the repository's existing tests. When a pin is ahead of or
+diverges from its upstream branch, retain it until the branch contains it, or
+make a reviewed manual transition. Do not fall back to an unguarded update when
+the check fails.
+
+### Check the final lock before publishing
+
+Save the workflow's original lock outside the checkout. After commit hooks and
+tests have run, export `HEAD:flake.lock` and compare that committed snapshot
+against the same baseline. This checks the lockfile that Git will publish:
+
+```bash
+set -euo pipefail
+baseline=$(mktemp)
+cp flake.lock "$baseline"
+confctl inputs update --forward-only --commit --no-changelog nixpkgs
+# Run the repository's required checks here.
+final_lock=$(mktemp)
+git show HEAD:flake.lock > "$final_lock"
+confctl inputs check-update --old-lock "$baseline" --new-lock "$final_lock"
+# Publish only after every preceding command succeeded.
+```
+
+`check-update` reads both lock files and applies the same complete-graph policy.
+It does not invoke Nix, install a lock or commit. Its exit statuses are the same
+as guarded update statuses. It can run without confctl cluster outputs.
+
+Use an ordinary non-force Git push after successful checks. If the target branch
+moved, retry in a new checkout from a fresh baseline so a
+concurrent manual pin is included in the next check. An ancestry check against a
+stale local baseline does not establish safety against a changed remote branch.

+require 'confctl/inputs/lock_graph'
+require 'confctl/inputs/git_compare'
+
+module ConfCtl
+  module Inputs
+    class ForwardGuard
+      Result = Struct.new(:status, :changes, :issues) do
+        def success? = %i[unchanged updated].include?(status)
+        def rejected? = status == :rejected
+        def error? = status == :error
+      end
+
+      Change = Struct.new(:path, :old_node, :new_node) do
+        def old_rev = old_node&.dig('locked', 'rev')
+        def new_rev = new_node&.dig('locked', 'rev')
+      end
+
+      class UnsupportedSource < StandardError; end
+
+      def initialize(provider: GitCompare.new)
+        @provider = provider
+      end
+
+      def validate(old_lock, candidate_lock)
+        old_entries = LockGraph.new(old_lock).entries
+        new_entries = LockGraph.new(candidate_lock).entries
+        changes = []
+        rejected = []
+        errors = []
+        cache = {}
+
+        (old_entries.keys | new_entries.keys).sort.each do |path|
+          old_node = old_entries[path]&.node
+          new_node = new_entries[path]&.node
+          next if same_source?(old_node, new_node)
+
+          change = Change.new(path: path, old_node: old_node, new_node: new_node)
+          changes << change
+          check_change(change, rejected, cache)
+        rescue UnsupportedSource, GitCompare::Error => e
+          errors << "#{path}: #{e.message}"
+        end
+
+        status = if !errors.empty?
+                   :error
+                 elsif !rejected.empty?
+                   :rejected
+                 elsif changes.empty?
+                   :unchanged
+                 else
+                   :updated
+                 end
+        Result.new(status: status, changes: changes, issues: errors + rejected)
+      rescue LockGraph::Error => e
+        Result.new(status: :error, changes: [], issues: [e.message])
+      end
+
+      protected
+
+      def same_source?(old_node, new_node)
+        old_node && new_node && old_node['locked'] == new_node['locked'] &&
+          old_node.fetch('flake', true) == new_node.fetch('flake', true)
+      end
+
+      def check_change(change, rejected, cache)
+        if change.new_node.nil?
+          rejected << "#{change.path}: previously reachable dependency was removed"
+          return
+        end
+
+        new_source = source(change.new_node)
+        return if change.old_node.nil?
+
+        old_source = source(change.old_node)
+        if old_source != new_source || change.old_node.fetch('flake', true) != change.new_node.fetch('flake', true)
+          rejected << "#{change.path}: source or extraction attributes changed; manual review required"
+          return
+        end
+
+        if change.old_rev == change.new_rev
+          rejected << "#{change.path}: locked attributes changed at the same revision"
+          return
+        end
+
+        key = [old_source, change.old_rev, change.new_rev]
+        outcome = cache.fetch(key) do
+          cache[key] = begin
+            @provider.compare(
+              owner: change.new_node['locked']['owner'], repo: change.new_node['locked']['repo'],
+              old_rev: change.old_rev, new_rev: change.new_rev
+            )
+          rescue GitCompare::Error => e
+            e
+          end
+        end
+        raise outcome if outcome.is_a?(GitCompare::Error)
+
+        return if outcome == :ahead
+
+        unless %i[behind diverged].include?(outcome)
+          raise GitCompare::Error, 'Unknown ancestry comparison outcome'
+        end
+
+        rejected << "#{change.path}: #{change.old_rev} -> #{change.new_rev} is #{outcome}"
+      end
+
+      def source(node)

+        unless locked['type'] == 'github' && [nil, 'github.com'].include?(locked['host']) &&

+                 value = locked[key]
+                 value.is_a?(String) && GitCompare::NAME.match?(value) && !%w[. ..].include?(value)
+               end
+          raise UnsupportedSource, 'Changed dependency is not a supported github.com source'
+        end
+        unless locked['rev'].is_a?(String) && GitCompare::SHA.match?(locked['rev'])
+          raise UnsupportedSource, 'Changed dependency lacks a full immutable Git revision'
+        end
+
+        allowed = %w[type owner repo host rev narHash lastModified dir]
+        unless (locked.keys - allowed).empty? &&
+               (!locked.has_key?('dir') || locked['dir'].is_a?(String)) &&
+               (!locked.has_key?('narHash') || locked['narHash'].is_a?(String)) &&
+               (!locked.has_key?('lastModified') || locked['lastModified'].is_a?(Integer))
+          raise UnsupportedSource, 'Unsupported GitHub source attributes'
+        end

+        locked.except('rev', 'narHash', 'lastModified').merge(
+          'owner' => locked['owner'].downcase, 'repo' => locked['repo'].downcase, 'host' => 'github.com'

+require 'confctl/git_repo_mirror'
+
+module ConfCtl
+  module Inputs
+    class GitCompare
+      class Error < StandardError; end
+
+      SHA = GitRepoMirror::SHA
+      NAME = /\A[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\z/
+
+      def compare(owner:, repo:, old_rev:, new_rev:)
+        unless [owner, repo].all? { |value| value.is_a?(String) && NAME.match?(value) && !%w[. ..].include?(value) } &&
+               [old_rev, new_rev].all? { |value| value.is_a?(String) && SHA.match?(value) }
+          raise Error, 'Git comparison requires a repository and full commit SHAs'
+        end
+        return :identical if old_rev == new_rev
+
+        # Preserve the locked spelling and exact URL used by FlakeLock and
+        # changelogs, so existing full mirrors share their objects and lock.
+        GitRepoMirror.new("https://github.com/#{owner}/#{repo}", quiet: true).compare(old_rev, new_rev)
+      rescue GitRepoMirror::Error => e
+        raise Error, e.message
+      end
+    end
+  end
+end

+        process_lock = git!('rev-parse', '--git-path', 'confctl-input-update.lock').strip

+module ConfCtl
+  module Inputs
+    # A semantic view of a version-7 lock, independent of generated node IDs.
+    class LockGraph
+      class Error < StandardError; end
+
+      Entry = Struct.new(:path, :node, :terminal_path)
+
+      attr_reader :entries
+
+      def initialize(lock)
+        @data = lock.respond_to?(:data) ? lock.data : lock
+        unless @data.is_a?(Hash) && @data['version'].eql?(7) && @data['nodes'].is_a?(Hash)
+          raise Error, 'Expected a version-7 flake lock graph'
+        end
+
+        @nodes = @data['nodes']
+        @root = @data['root']
+        node!(@root)
+        @entries = {}
+        walk([], @root, [@root])
+      end
+
+      def resolve_path(path)
+        components = path.is_a?(String) ? path.split('/', -1) : path
+        validate_path!(components)
+        id, terminal = resolve(components, [])
+        Entry.new(path: components.join('/'), node: node!(id), terminal_path: terminal.join('/'))
+      end
+
+      def update_inputs(names)
+        names.map { |name| resolve_path(name).terminal_path }.uniq
+      end
+
+      protected
+
+      def node!(id)
+        node = @nodes[id]
+        unless id.is_a?(String) && node.is_a?(Hash) &&
+               (!node.has_key?('inputs') || node['inputs'].is_a?(Hash)) &&
+               (id == @root || node['locked'].is_a?(Hash)) &&
+               (!node.has_key?('original') || node['original'].is_a?(Hash)) &&
+               (!node.has_key?('flake') || [true, false].include?(node['flake']))
+          raise Error, 'Malformed or dangling lock graph node'
+        end
+
+        validate_path!((node['inputs'] || {}).keys)
+        node
+      end
+
+      def validate_path!(path)
+        return if path.is_a?(Array) && path.all? { |name| name.is_a?(String) && !name.empty? && !name.include?('/') }
+
+        raise Error, 'Malformed lock input path'
+      end
+
+      def resolve(components, stack)
+        id = @root
+        terminal = []
+        components.each do |name|
+          key = [id, name]
+          raise Error, 'Cyclic follows reference in lock graph' if stack.include?(key)
+
+          edge = (node!(id)['inputs'] || {})[name]
+          case edge
+          when String
+            id = edge
+            node!(id)
+            terminal << name
+          when Array
+            validate_path!(edge)
+            id, terminal = resolve(edge, stack + [key])
+          else
+            raise Error, 'Malformed or dangling lock input reference'
+          end
+        end
+        [id, terminal]
+      end
+
+      def walk(prefix, id, ancestors)
+        (node!(id)['inputs'] || {}).keys.sort.each do |name|
+          validate_path!([name])
+          path = prefix + [name]
+          entry = resolve_path(path)
+          target, = resolve(path, [])
+          raise Error, 'Cyclic dependency in lock graph' if ancestors.include?(target)
+
+          @entries[entry.path] = entry
+          walk(path, target, ancestors + [target])
+        end
+      end
+    end
+  end
+end

+use strict;

    ci: guard automated flake updates
    
    Use the exact shared confctl CI package to reject input updates that lose
    previously pinned ancestry. Keep the deployment-tool input unchanged and
    retain the existing channel selections and changelog policy.
    
    Save the original lock before updates and validate the committed final
    lock snapshot before an ordinary push. Preserve the configuration shell
    for Ruby hooks, install the declared hooks and select the new guard tool
    explicitly. Refresh imported actions to current hosted-runner releases.
    
    Reuse confctl's Git mirrors between runs, including rejected updates. A
    restored cache never skips the ancestry checks.
